Published Nov. 18, 2026 By Kristin Jensen Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Pfizer will work with Starna Therapeutics to develop "in vivo" cell therapies for autoimmune disease. Jeenah Moon via Getty Images Dive Brief: Pfizer is undertaking yet another deal in China to get into a budding area of research, using “in vivo” cell therapy for autoimmune diseases. Under the terms of the agreement with Starna Therapeutics, Pfizer will obtain exclusive rights outside Greater China to three preclinical programs focused on autoimmune diseases. It will also get the rights to use Starna’s technology in inflammation, immunology and oncology as well as options to license other projects and expand its territory to include Greater China. Pfizer will pay Starna $330 million up front and offer as much as $2.3 billion more in payments for reaching certain development and commercial milestones. Though this would be its first venture into this particular area of research, the company on Wednesday emphasized its experience with RNA-based medicines after the success of the COVID-19 vaccine Comirnaty. Pfizer said it would manufacture the products for clinical trials in the U.S. Starna is developing RNA medicines that are designed to reprogram cells inside the body — or “in vivo” — while also branching into fields beyond oncology. Marketed CAR-T cell cancer therapies such as Johnson & Johnson’s Carvykti use an “ex vivo” process that involves harvesting a patient’s cells, modifying them and infusing them back into the body. Drugmakers like Starna are hoping that they can eliminate much of the complicated and lengthy process involved in making an ex vivo CAR-T therapy as well as avoid the chemotherapy “conditioning” that typically accompanies it. The in vivo work is still in early stages, but it’s drawn a lot of attention. Just in the last two years, AstraZeneca, AbbVie, Gilead Sciences and Bristol Myers Squibb have all undertaken acquisitions centered on the technology. Eli Lilly, meanwhile, has announced two buyouts this year alone. Many drugmakers are now pursuing a similar strategy to Pfizer and Starna’s, hoping that the therapies can treat conditions such as lupus and multiple sclerosis in addition to cancer. Research released a few years ago suggested that CAR-T treatments can “reset” the immune system, and ex vivo therapies are getting closer to market for that use. But there are also questions; Novartis and Bristol Myers both recently paused trials of CAR-T therapies in autoimmune conditions because of safety concerns. For Pfizer, the Starna deal marks at least the fifth major alliance with a Chinese company since the start of 2025, and the company is far from alone in pursuing drug candidates in the country. The trend has become so pronounced that the industry trade group BIO recently unveiled a five-year plan to help prop up the U.S. biotechnology industry in the face of Chinese competition. Dupixent generated €5.7 billion in Q3 revenue (~40% of group sales), making the early-2030s patent cliff the central strategic driver for external growth. Original reporting follows.Original story from November 20, 2026: Sanofi is evaluating a potential acquisition of U.S. drugmaker Insmed, according to a Bloomberg report published November 19, with the French pharma giant working with advisers to assess a deal that could be valued between $35 billion and $43 billion. If completed at the high end of that range, it would rank as the largest biopharma buyout since Pfizer’s $43 billion acquisition of Seagen in 2023.Neither company has commented on the report, which cited anonymous sources. Insmed shares surged roughly 18% to $141.87 on the news, while Sanofi shares slipped about 2% to $46.15.The strategic logic centers on Dupixent, Sanofi’s blockbuster biologic for inflammatory conditions including eczema and asthma, which generated €5.7 billion in third-quarter revenue — nearly 40% of Sanofi’s total group sales. The drug is on track toward patent expiration in the early 2030s, leaving a significant revenue hole that CEO Belén Garijo has repeatedly flagged as the company’s defining challenge. Garijo has told investors the organization is squarely focused on managing the post-Dupixent transition over the next decade, with M&A and licensing alongside improved R&D productivity as the primary levers. Getty Images Dive Brief: The Food and Drug Administration has approved the first drug for a type of inherited disorder, endorsing BridgeBio’s Welgemda for the 2I/R9 variant of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy characterized by muscle breakdown due to an enzyme deficiency. Approval of Welgemda expands BridgeBio’s portfolio of marketed drugs, joining the rare heart-disease drug Attruby as a commercial-stage product. if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); Dive Insight: Formerly known as BBP-418 and scientifically as ribitol, Welgemda is for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, in which weakness in the shoulders and hips leads to atrophy in the arms and legs. In the 2I/R9 variant that Welgemda specifically treats, a genetic mutation leads to a shortage of an enzyme called FKRP essential to a chemical process that stabilizes muscle cells. In people with this disorder, limb weakness is seen first in childhood or early adulthood, but the disease can progress to cause heart and lung problems. About 7,000 people in the U.S. and Europe have the 2I/R9 disorder and related forms of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, according to BridgeBio. Welgemda’s mechanism of action “is not fully known,” according to the FDA, but it is believed that it helps increase a natural sugar molecule that anchors a key protein in muscle tissue. It is taken twice a day as an oral solution mixed with water. In the Phase 3 clinical trial, BridgeBio tested Welgemda against a placebo to detect differences in the chemical reaction that FKRP is essential to, as well as time over a 100-meter walking test and a breathing diagnostic. People who received Welgemda had a statistically significant benefit on all three after 12 months of treatment, notably the walking test, where people who got the drug were 0.27 meters per second faster than those who got the placebo. The most common side effect was diarrhea, and no trial enrollee who got Welgemda quit because of side effects. BridgeBio executives told Wall Street analysts they have identified 500 genetically confirmed patients in the U.S., hoping to reach 100 by the end of 2027, 300 by the end of 2028 and all 500 by the end of 2029. The executive team also believes there are 2,000 to 3,000 U.S. patients overall who will need to be identified by patient awareness and genetic testing campaigns. When patients in Europe and other countries are included, the total peak sales could be as high as $1.5 billion, according to T.D. Cowen analyst Tyler Van Buren. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Rise and shine, everyone, another busy day is on the way. And it is getting off to a pleasant start here on the Pharmalot campus, where clear blue skies and comfy breezes are greeting us. As for the official mascots, they have finished keeping passersby at bay and are now happily snoozing in their respective corners. As for us, we are firing up the trusty kettle for another cup of stimulation. Our choice today is peppermint, an old standby from our pantry. Of course, you are invited to join us. Meanwhile, here is the latest menu of tidbits. As always, do keep in touch. And best of luck today. … Merck and Isomorphic Labs, the artificial intelligence drug designer built on a Nobel-winning technology that can model how molecules will bind to proteins, are entering into a research collaboration to discover small molecule candidates for an undisclosed oncology target of “strategic importance,” STAT reports. The partnership — only the latest such deal between a pharma giant and Isomorphic — will join Isomorphic’s proprietary drug design engine and existing wet lab data from Merck, which will handle the preclinical and clinical development, manufacturing, and commercializing of any products. Advertisement The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved a Sanofi drug, making ​it the first treatment for a ‌type of rare genetic condition that affects the brain and nervous system, Reuters writes. The drug, ​branded as Infilbray, was approved for ​adults and children weighing at least ⁠15 kilograms, or about 33 pounds, ​with type 3 Gaucher disease, a ​rare inherited disorder that causes fatty substances to build up in the body and brain. The ​approval was based on a late-stage ​study of 43 patients aged 12 years and ‌older ⁠whose symptoms outside the brain and nervous system had been stabilized with enzyme replacement therapy. title: Argenx to buy peptide platform in potentially billion-dollar deal
content: An article from Dive Brief Argenx to buy peptide platform in potentially billion-dollar deal For $550 million up front, Argenx will take control of Unnatural Products’ “macrocyclic peptide” technology and direct it to develop oral, durable medicines for serious immune-mediated diseases. Published Nov. 9, 2026 Jacob Bell Lead Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Argenx agreed to acquire Unnatural Products, a maker of "macrocyclic peptides," on Nov. 9, 2026. deliormanli via Getty Images Dive Brief: Argenx, a Netherlands-based biotechnology company focused on antibody drugs, on Monday said it has agreed to acquire a protein specialist in a potentially billion-dollar-plus deal. Unnatural Products has a platform that pairs machine learning, screening and other techniques to engineer “macrocyclic peptides.” These peptides are larger and more complex than typical small molecules, which allows them to more effectively bind to tricky proteins and address some challenging diseases. Yet, they’re still tiny enough that they can be swallowed. Argenx plans to use the platform to develop oral, durable medicines for serious immune-mediated diseases. The acquisition carries a $550 million upfront cash payment. Unnatural Products could receive up to $595 million more if specific milestones are hit. Argenx was drawn in as well, having already taken a minority stake in Unnatural Products before pursuing a full buyout. In a statement, Argenx CEO Karen Massey said these macrocyclic peptide capabilities are “highly complementary” to her own company’s antibody engineering. “After working together for more than two years, we also know there is a strong fit in how we work: science first, entrepreneurial and focused on patients,” Massey added. “We want to preserve what has made [Unnatural Products] successful while bringing the strengths of both teams together.” The Food and Drug Administration has already approved at least a handful of macrocyclic peptide therapies. In 2020, for example, Rhythm Pharmaceuticals’ Imcivree was cleared as a treatment for certain genetic forms of obesity. The following year, Aurinia Pharmaceuticals’ Lupkynis became the first-ever oral medicine for adults with active lupus nephritis. In 2023, the FDA greenlit a UCB medicine called Zilbrysq for “generalized myasthenia gravis,” a rare autoimmune condition that’s become somewhat of a battleground for several developers. Argenx’s own flagship product, Vyvgart, targets this disease and brought in $4.5 billion in net product sales from January through the end of September. Thomas Smith, a Leerink Partners analyst who covers Argenx, wrote in a note to clients that the new acquisition “represents potential for longer-term strategic value.” He explained there’s a desire — both in big pharma and in the broader immunology and inflammation research space — to make oral, long-acting therapeutics that are able to be more effective and convenient than conventional biologics. The Unnatural Products deal, which comes on the heels of Argenx’s potentially $2.2 billion purchase of Forte Biosciences, also “signals further focus on pipeline growth and diversification,” Smith wrote. title: 科济药业公布体内CAR-T首次临床数据！CT1182针对R/R B-NHL初步ORR达83.3%
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 科济药业公布体内CAR-T首次临床数据！CT1182针对R/R B-NHL初步ORR达83.3% 科济药业公布体内CAR-T首次临床数据！CT1182针对R/R B-NHL初步ORR达83.3% 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 19小时前 1071 科济药业 CT1182 临床数据 CD19/CD20 CAR-T 体内CAR-T赛道再迎重要进展。11月22日，科济药业公布了自主研发的靶向CD19/CD20体内CAR-T候选产品 CT1182（KJ-C2529）的首次临床数据。该产品基于CARvivo™平台开发，用于治疗复发/难治性B细胞非霍奇金淋巴瘤（R/R B-NHL）。图源：科济药业企业公告截至2026年10月31日，中位随访约3.2个月，6例可评估患者中已有5例达到缓解，包括3例完全缓解（CR）和2例部分缓解（PR），初步客观缓解率（ORR）为83.3%。所有缓解均在持续中，最长缓解时间接近5个月。值得关注的是，CT1182在起始剂量下即观察到CR。在患者均为Ann Arbor IV期侵袭性淋巴瘤、中位既往治疗3线的情况下，这组早期数据展现出一定的临床潜力。一、6例患者5例缓解，起始剂量即观察到CR体内CAR-T无需采集患者T细胞进行体外改造，而是通过载体将CAR基因直接递送至体内T细胞，使其在患者体内生成CAR-T细胞，有望简化传统CAR-T的制备流程，并降低治疗成本。此次KJ-C2529公布的早期数据，首先展现了其在R/R B-NHL中的初步疗效。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库截至2026年10月31日，KJ-C2529剂量探索范围为1.2×10⁸ TU至7.2×10⁸ TU，共纳入6例患者，包括5例弥漫大B细胞淋巴瘤（DLBCL）和1例母细胞型套细胞淋巴瘤（MCL）。从患者基线来看，6例患者均为侵袭性淋巴瘤亚型，全部处于Ann Arbor IV期，中位既往治疗3线，中位总肿瘤负荷（SPD）为1,927.5 mm²。其中，2例患者既往接受过T细胞特异性双抗治疗。在这样的患者人群中，KJ-C2529取得了3例CR、2例PR的初步疗效。尤其是起始剂量1.2×10⁸ TU即观察到CR，最长缓解持续时间已接近5个月，且所有缓解在数据截止时仍在持续。随着后续剂量探索和随访时间延长，其疗效表现仍有待进一步观察。双抗经治患者的表现也提供了值得关注的线索：2例患者中，1例获得CR；另一例则因T细胞耗竭及CD20抗原丢失，未观察到有效的CAR-T扩增。这一差异提示，体内CAR-T的治疗效果不仅与载体递送效率有关，也可能受到患者自身T细胞功能状态及肿瘤靶抗原表达的影响。二、0例IRR、0例DLT，完全B细胞清除拓展应用想象空间除了疗效，KJ-C2529的初步安全性表现同样值得关注。在6例患者中，未观察到治疗相关严重不良事件（SAE）、剂量限制性毒性（DLT）及输注相关反应（IRR），也未出现免疫效应细胞相关神经毒性综合征（ICANS）、免疫效应细胞相关噬血细胞性淋巴组织细胞增多症样综合征（IEC-HS）及与输注相关的细胞因子双相增高，仅出现1级细胞因子释放综合征（CRS）。血液学毒性总体较轻。除1例无法完全排除与疾病相关的3级白细胞减少外，未发生其他与治疗相关的3级及以上血液学毒性。其中，未观察到IRR及严重免疫相关毒性，为KJ-C2529后续探索更便捷的给药和治疗管理模式提供了积极信号。不过，目前样本量仅为6例，其安全性仍需更大规模临床研究验证。另一项值得关注的结果是，所有达到缓解的患者均观察到完全B细胞清除。这一现象也让KJ-C2529未来的应用探索不再局限于血液肿瘤。近年来，CAR-T在自身免疫性疾病领域的研究持续推进，深度清除异常B细胞是相关治疗策略的重要方向。KJ-C2529此次观察到的B细胞清除结果，为其未来向自身免疫性疾病等B细胞相关疾病拓展提供了初步依据，但具体疗效仍有待临床研究验证。下一步，KJ-C2529将进一步扩大剂量探索范围，明确潜在的推荐II期剂量（RP2D）及剂量－反应关系，预计于2027年上半年申报注册临床试验。从首次披露的人体数据来看，KJ-C2529已初步展现出体内CAR-T的临床应用潜力。随着后续研究推进，其疗效持续性、安全性及适应症拓展空间值得持续关注。参考来源：[1] 国产IgA肾病创新药研发再迎新进展！11月17日，CDE官网显示，华东医药旗下1类创新生物药HDM4002注射液获批临床，拟用于治疗具有疾病进展风险的原发性免疫球蛋白A（IgA）肾病成人患者，以减少肾功能损失。图源：华东医药企业公告与此同时，华东医药旗下多款产品及合作产品被纳入2026年新版国家医保药品目录及商业健康保险创新药品目录，研发与商业化两端均有新进展。一、全球首款CFB/MASP-2双抗，瞄准IgA肾病HDM4002由杭州中美华东制药有限公司研发并拥有全球知识产权，是一款1类生物新药。IgA肾病的发生发展与免疫异常及补体系统过度激活密切相关。其中，补体旁路途径（AP）和凝集素途径（LP）是重要的疾病相关通路，CFB和MASP-2分别参与这两条通路的激活，也是当前补体靶向治疗的重要研究靶点。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库目前，针对CFB或MASP-2的单靶点药物已在IgA肾病领域展开临床探索。与之不同，HDM4002采用单分子双靶点设计，可同时靶向CFB和MASP-2，干预补体旁路途径与凝集素途径，旨在从两条补体激活通路入手，实现双重阻断，为IgA肾病治疗提供新的研发思路。从企业研发管线来看，华东医药今年以来也有多款创新药取得进展。据摩熵医药数据库显示，截至目前，华东医药已有4款1类新药进入获批临床及以上研发阶段。其中，HDM4002注射液、注射用HDM-2024均为今年首次获批临床的1类新药，目前HDM-2024已进入晚期实体瘤Ⅰ期临床研究阶段。 Published Nov. 23, 2026 Jonathan Gardner Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images Dive Brief: A protein degrading eczema drug developed by Kymera Therapeutics met the main goals of a Phase 2 clinical trial, significantly reducing disease severity in enrollees who got it compared with those given a placebo, the company said Monday. Codenamed KT-621, the drug demonstrated efficacy comparable to injectable biologics like Sanofi and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals’ Dupixent, according to Wall Street analysts. One of the tested doses achieved an average 72% reduction on an eczema severity scale after 16 weeks, 45 percentage points greater than in enrollees who got a placebo. Kymera said it plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in eczema — also called atopic dermatitis — by mid-2027, while a Phase 2 trial in asthma is expected to read out by late next year. Dupixent is in its 10th year on the market and is due to lose patent-protected exclusivity in the U.S. in 2032. KT-621, therefore, must compete not just with Dupixent and other biologics like Eli Lilly’s Ebglyss, but also any biosimilars that can be expected to soon enter the market after key patents expire. With KT-621, Kymera is seeking to tamp down the same inflammatory processes as Dupixent and Ebglyss. But instead of blocking signaling proteins related to allergic conditions, it degrades a transcription factor on the same pathway by triggering cellular trash disposal systems. The trial Kymera reported today, titled BROADEN2, enrolled 244 people and randomized them into four roughly equal-sized groups to take one of three doses of KT-621 or a placebo. The primary goal was the score on a scale called the Eczema Area and Severity Index, or EASI. The best score of 72% reduction came from the people who got the mid-dose, with the low-dose group seeing their EASI scores drop 64% and the high dose 61%. As a secondary goal, the trial also measured the proportion of patients who had a 75% reduction in their EASI scores. In the mid-dose group, 62% achieved this mark, compared with 22% of the placebo group. The drug also appeared safe, with most side effects proving mild or moderate. Higher rates of conjunctivitis, a known side effect, were detected in the people receiving the study drug, but none of the people who got it quit taking the drug. Four other serious adverse events were reported, though none were judged to be related to the drug. Wall Street analysts said the data show KT-621 has “biologic-like efficacy,” putting it in a position to challenge Dupixent and related medicines. “Overall, we believe the balance of topline data is strongly supportive of an effective oral treatment option with clean safety/tolerability — a uniquely competitive profile across the [eczema] field, capable of both taking share and expanding the addressable market,” wrote Leerink Research analyst Thomas Smith in a client note. 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 昨天 11:51 1787 TYK2 翰森制药集团有限公司 银屑病 HS-10374 片 CMS-D001片 11月20日，CDE官网显示，翰森制药自主研发的1类新药 氘索昔替尼（HS-10374）上市申请获受理，拟用于治疗成人中重度斑块状银屑病。这也是国产首个申报上市的TYK2变构抑制剂。图源：CDE官网HS-10374是一款口服高选择性TYK2变构抑制剂，可抑制白细胞介素-12（IL-12）、IL-23及I型干扰素（IFN）通路的信号传导，在多种自身免疫性疾病领域具有潜在治疗价值。一、Ⅲ期临床达到主要终点，近1/3患者实现PASI 100今年9月，翰森制药宣布，HS-10374治疗成人中重度斑块状银屑病的Ⅲ期临床研究达到共同主要终点及多项次要终点。研究结果显示，治疗第16周，HS-10374组达到银屑病面积和严重程度指数较基线改善至少75%（PASI 75）的患者比例，以及达到静态医师整体评估评分0或1、且较基线至少改善2分（sPGA 0/1）的患者比例，均显著高于安慰剂组。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库更值得关注的是，在第16周，HS-10374组超过半数患者达到PASI 90应答，近1/3患者达到PASI 100应答，展现出较好的皮损改善效果。安全性方面，HS-10374表现出良好的安全性和耐受性，其安全性特征与同类TYK2抑制剂类似，未观察到新的安全性信号。二、国产TYK2赛道升温，多款新药进入后期临床TYK2是JAK激酶家族的重要成员，参与IL-12、IL-23及I型干扰素等多种细胞因子的信号传导。通过选择性抑制TYK2相关信号通路，有望在调节异常免疫反应的同时，为银屑病等自身免疫性疾病提供新的口服治疗选择。从全球研发格局来看，目前已获批上市的选择性TYK2抑制剂仅有一款，即百时美施贵宝（BMS）的氘可来昔替尼（Deucravacitinib）。此外，武田的zasocitinib已于今年9月在美国申报上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库国内企业也在加快TYK2抑制剂的研发推进。除翰森制药的HS-10374外，益方生物的nomelcitinib（D-2570）已完成Ⅲ期临床研究，尚未递交上市申请；北京诺诚健华的fadeucravacitinib也已顺利完成Ⅲ期临床研究；海思科的envudeucitinib（ESK-001）已授权Alumis，Ⅲ期临床研究取得积极进展。此外，据摩熵医药数据库显示，国内还有多款TYK2抑制剂进入Ⅱ期临床阶段，包括康哲药业的CMS-D001、微芯生物的CS-32582、祐森健恒的UA-021、上海致根医药的ZG-002及安锐生物的ARTS-011等。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库三、结语随着HS-10374率先递交上市申请，国产TYK2变构抑制剂开始向商业化阶段迈进。未来，随着更多候选药物陆续完成临床开发并推进上市，TYK2抑制剂在银屑病等自身免疫性疾病领域的竞争有望进一步加剧。 title: STAT Plus: Kymera Therapeutics reports mid-stage eczema trial success for would-be Dupixent rival
content: STAT PlusBiotech Kymera Therapeutics reports mid-stage eczema trial success for would-be Dupixent rival Study was seen as one of this year’s most impactful immunology drug readouts Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Eczema is defined by patches of itchy, dry, and bumpy skin that flare due to immune inflammation.Adobe By Jonathan WosenNov. 23, 2026 West Coast Biotech & Life Sciences Reporter Jonathan Wosen[email protected]Jonathan Wosen is STAT’s West Coast biotech & life sciences reporter. You can reach Jonathan on Signal at jwosen.27. In a closely watched trial seen as one of this year’s most impactful immunology drug readouts, Kymera Therapeutics announced on Monday that its experimental therapy effectively and safely treated eczema patients’ itchy, inflamed skin. In the Phase 2 trial, moderate-to-severe eczema patients randomly assigned to receive the biotech’s pill, KT-621, showed a statistically significant reduction in disease severity compared with those given a placebo. This was true across all three doses tested after 16 weeks of treatment, with a peak placebo-adjusted improvement of 45% among those given a moderate dose. Patients on this dose were also more likely to see an improvement of 75% or more in disease severity, with 62% of treated participants clearing that bar compared with 22% of the placebo group.Advertisement The BROADEN2 trial succeeded across all primary and secondary endpoints, including itch reduction and the fraction of patients who achieved clear or almost-clear skin. KT-621 was also generally safe and well tolerated. The only side effect that was more common among patients on the drug was conjunctivitis (i.e. pink eye), which appeared in 20%, 13%, and 11% of patients on a low, middle, and high dose, respectively. Those issues — which included violations of study blinding protocols and after-the-fact changes to the statistical analysis plan — compromised Capricor’s findings, the FDA said. “This was not a decision made lightly. Upholding rigorous evidentiary standards is precisely how the FDA protects patients, particularly those living with rare diseases, from interventions whose benefits have not been sufficiently established,” the regulator added. “We stand behind the rigor of our clinical program and the integrity of our data, and we believe the data support approval,” countered CEO Linda Marbán, in Capricor’s statement. “We are reviewing the letter carefully and will share next steps once we have completed our evaluation.” Deramiocel is made from donor-derived heart cells able to preserve certain cardiac and muscle function. Capricor aimed for an approval based on results from a small trial and data from a historical study of heart function. Yet in July 2025, FDA officials rejected deramiocel, saying the company hadn't proven the therapy’s effectiveness and needed additional data. Capricor claimed to have been blindsided by the ruling. “We are surprised by this decision by the FDA,” Marbán said in a statement at the time. In briefing documents ahead of the meeting, FDA scientists argued deramiocel had actually failed the trial and tinkered with statistical analyses to produce a more compelling story. The advisory committee ultimately sided with the FDA's assessment, with a majority of panelists concluding testing hadn't shown clear evidence of deramiocel's effectiveness. Panelists instead expressed more support for its potential impact on upper limb function. The FDA, which originally sought to respond to Capricor by late August, extended its review of deramiocel to Nov. 22 after Capricor said it would instead seek clearance in a “refined” indication “focused on upper limb function.” More than two dozen trial investigators and physicians also penned a letter of support for approval to regulators in recent weeks. Deramiocel’s review is “clearly a case where regulatory flexibility can be applied,” that group wrote. Rejection “would signal complete inflexibility on the part of the agency, contradicting the core values articulated” by its stance on rare disease drug reviews. Under previous FDA leadership, a handful of drugmakers claimed to have been stunned by a sudden shift in regulatory guidance. Yet since the resignations of ex-commissioner Marty Makary and top deputy Vinay Prasad, U.S. regulators have changed their stance on a number of these decisions. The Food and Drug Administration said Friday that it had rejected a cell therapy intended for patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy developed by Capricor Therapeutics. The decision to block the treatment, called deramiocel, from reaching the market should have been an easy one for regulators to make. The targeted patient population — teenagers and young men with Duchenne who had already lost the ability to walk — have few treatment options today. Deramiocel didn’t help them either. Capricor conducted two randomized clinical trials. Both failed to show deramiocel could stave off heart failure or preserve muscle function in their arms. For the first time in more than a year, the Food and Drug Administration has sent notices to companies for failing to report required clinical trial information. The agency sends such notices when a trial sponsor fails to comply with a federal law that requires studies to be registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, a federal government database, within 21 days after the first human subject is enrolled. Summary results must also be posted to the database within 12 months after the trial’s primary completion date.Advertisement The FDA, however, has rarely sent noncompliance letters, despite years of criticism over lax enforcement. In recent years, calls for greater transparency have sparked a raft of studies showing a failure by drug companies, universities, and academic medical centers to comply with disclosure requirements. content: STAT PlusPharma FDA approves new breast cancer drug, providing new option for some patients, boost for Roche Company believes therapy could become its top-selling product, though estimates vary Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Xavier GALIANA/AFP via Getty Images By Andrew JosephNov. 16, 2026 Europe Correspondent Andrew Joseph[email protected]Andrew covers the biopharma industry, scientific research, and public health across the continent. You can reach Andrew confidentially on Signal at drewqjoseph.71. The Food and Drug Administration on Monday approved a new breast cancer drug from Roche, teeing up the launch of a medicine that the Swiss company has said could become its top-selling product ever. The approval of Wilserdly, also known as giredestrant, was one of the most important regulatory decisions Roche had been awaiting. It also gives the company another foothold in breast cancer treatments, a field in which it has a storied history with the drug Herceptin through its subsidiary Genentech, though in recent years it’s fallen behind rival pharma companies in oncology. Advertisement The approval is specifically for patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that has picked up a mutation in the ESR1 gene, a sign that the tumor is developing resistance to standard treatments. The evERA trial showed that the drug, an oral treatment known as a selective estrogen receptor degrader, or SERD, extended the time period before patients’ tumors progressed. Adam Feuerstein[email protected]Adam Feuerstein is a senior writer and biotech columnist, reporting on the crossroads of drug development, business, Wall Street, and biotechnology. He is also a co-host of the weekly biotech podcast The Readout Loud and author of the newsletter Adam’s Biotech Scorecard. You can reach Adam on Signal at stataf.54. The Food and Drug Administration rejected a treatment for a type of lung cancer developed by the U.S.-based biotech Summit Therapeutics and the Chinese drugmaker Akeso, Summit said on Sunday. In a letter sent to the companies, FDA regulators said the drug, called ivonescimab, could not be approved because it didn’t help patients live longer. While the drug was found to slow lung cancer worsening in patients, the absence of a survival benefit “does not support the positive benefit-risk profile in support of approval,” FDA reviewers concluded. content: STAT PlusPharma In a win for MAHA, FDA creates new regulatory category for the supplement NAC NAC has been sold as a dietary supplement for years Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Margaret MantoNov. 16, 2026 Washington Correspondent Margaret Manto[email protected]Margaret is a Washington correspondent covering the Food and Drug Administration and other federal health agencies. Reach her on Signal at margaretmanto.61. WASHINGTON — The Food and Drug Administration is proposing a new classification for a product that’s existed in a legal gray area for years, a win for proponents of dietary supplements, including members of the MAHA movement. The proposed rule would classify N-acetyl-L-cysteine, known as NAC and already widely sold over the counter, as the agency’s first “Dietary Ingredient Not Excluded from the Dietary Supplement Definition” — in essence, not not a supplement. Advertisement The need for the legal backbending stems from the fact that the FDA previously approved NAC as a drug, and FDA regulations prohibit the agency from including approved drugs in the dietary supplement category. In 1963, the agency approved NAC to break up mucus in certain lung conditions, and in 1985 to treat acetaminophen overdose. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account?
